question: Which event does this illustration depict?
options: The parting of the Red Sea
ref_kjv: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
explanation: Genesis opens with God creating the heaven and the earth and then calling light into being.
hint: Think of the very first chapter of the Bible.

question: According to Genesis 1, what did God create on the first day?
ref_kjv: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light. And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.
explanation: On the first day God said "Let there be light" and divided the light from the darkness.

question: On which day does Genesis 1 describe the making of the sun, moon and stars?
ref_kjv: And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also. And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth, And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good. And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.
explanation: The "two great lights" and the stars are placed in the firmament on the fourth day.
hint: It comes after the dry land and plants.

question: On which day did God rest from all His work?
ref_kjv: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
explanation: Genesis 2:2 says God ended His work and rested on the seventh day.

question: Which Bible account does this scene show?
ref_kjv: And God spake unto Noah, saying, Go forth of the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ wives with thee. Bring forth with thee every living thing that is with thee, of all flesh, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth. And Noah went forth, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him: Every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl, and whatsoever creepeth upon the earth, after their kinds, went forth out of the ark.
explanation: After the flood God told Noah to bring every living creature out of the ark.

question: What sign of His covenant did God set in the clouds after the flood?
ref_kjv: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
explanation: God said, "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant."

question: Which bird returned to Noah with an olive leaf?
ref_kjv: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
explanation: The dove came back in the evening with an olive leaf, showing the waters were abating.
hint: Noah sent out two kinds of birds; this was the second.

question: On which mountains did the ark come to rest?
ref_kjv: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
explanation: Genesis 8:4 says the ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat.

question: What were the names of Noah's three sons?
ref_kjv: And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
explanation: Genesis 6:10 names Noah's sons as Shem, Ham and Japheth.

question: God told this patriarch to look toward heaven and number the stars. Who was he?
ref_kjv: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
explanation: God brought Abram outside and promised, "So shall thy seed be."

question: God promised that Abram's descendants would be as many as what?
ref_kjv: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
explanation: Genesis 15:5 compares Abram's descendants to the stars. (Genesis 22:17 also mentions the sand of the seashore.)

question: From which city did Terah's family, including Abram, set out?
ref_kjv: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter in law, his son Abram’s wife; and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan; and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.
explanation: Terah took Abram and Sarai and went forth from Ur of the Chaldees toward Canaan.

question: What new name did God give Abram?
ref_kjv: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee.
explanation: God said, "Thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee."

question: Which wife of Abraham bore Isaac in her old age?
ref_kjv: For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him. And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.
explanation: Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son, whom he named Isaac.

question: Which son received a special coat from his father Jacob (Israel)?
ref_kjv: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
explanation: Israel loved Joseph more than his other children and made him a coat of many colours.

question: To whom did Joseph's brothers sell him?
ref_kjv: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
explanation: The brothers drew Joseph out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmeelites, who took him to Egypt.

question: For how many pieces of silver was Joseph sold?
ref_kjv: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
explanation: Genesis 37:28 records the price as twenty pieces of silver.
hint: It is fewer than the price paid to Judas.

question: Whose dreams did Joseph interpret while he was in prison?
ref_kjv: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.
explanation: The butler and the baker of the king of Egypt both dreamed in prison, and Joseph interpreted their dreams.

question: In Pharaoh's dream, what came up out of the river, seven fat and seven lean?
ref_kjv: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow. And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river. And the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.
explanation: Pharaoh saw seven well-favoured kine followed by seven ill-favoured kine.

question: Which event does this illustration show?
ref_kjv: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided. And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
explanation: The waters were divided and Israel went into the midst of the sea upon dry ground.

question: What did Moses stretch out over the sea before it divided?
ref_kjv: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
explanation: Exodus 14:21: "Moses stretched out his hand over the sea." (Exodus 14:16 also mentions lifting up his rod.)

question: What went before Israel by night to give them light?
ref_kjv: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:
explanation: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud and by night in a pillar of fire.

question: Who was Moses' brother, appointed to speak for him?
ref_kjv: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
explanation: God named "Aaron the Levite thy brother" as the one who could speak well.

question: After the crossing, who took a timbrel and led the women in song?
ref_kjv: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.
explanation: Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand.

question: Who is the young shepherd facing the giant?
ref_kjv: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth. So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
explanation: David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone.

question: Goliath came from which Philistine city?
ref_kjv: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
explanation: 1 Samuel 17:4 calls him "Goliath, of Gath."

question: How many smooth stones did David choose from the brook?
ref_kjv: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
explanation: David chose five smooth stones out of the brook and put them in his shepherd's bag.

question: Which people did Goliath fight for?
ref_kjv: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
explanation: Goliath was a champion out of the camp of the Philistines.

question: In which valley did Israel face the Philistines?
ref_kjv: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and pitched by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
explanation: Saul and the men of Israel pitched by the valley of Elah.

question: Which king built and dedicated the first temple in Jerusalem?
ref_kjv: And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the LORD. And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto the LORD, two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.
explanation: Solomon and all Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.

question: What did Solomon ask God for at Gibeon?
ref_kjv: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
explanation: Solomon asked for "an understanding heart to judge thy people."

question: Which queen came to test Solomon with hard questions?
ref_kjv: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.
explanation: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to prove him with hard questions.

question: What names were given to the two bronze pillars of Solomon's temple porch?
ref_kjv: And he set up the pillars in the porch of the temple: and he set up the right pillar, and called the name thereof Jachin: and he set up the left pillar, and called the name thereof Boaz.
explanation: The right pillar was called Jachin and the left pillar Boaz.

question: What trees did Solomon ask Hiram's servants to cut from Lebanon?
ref_kjv: Now therefore command thou that they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be with thy servants: and unto thee will I give hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt appoint: for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.
explanation: Solomon asked Hiram to "hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon." (Hiram also supplied fir.)

question: Which prophet saw fire fall from heaven on Mount Carmel?
ref_kjv: And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word. Hear me, O LORD, hear me, that this people may know that thou art the LORD God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again. Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
explanation: After Elijah prayed, the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice.

question: Prophets of which god opposed Elijah on Mount Carmel?
ref_kjv: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.
explanation: Elijah asked Ahab to gather the prophets of Baal to Mount Carmel.

question: How many prophets of Baal were gathered to Mount Carmel?
ref_kjv: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.
explanation: 1 Kings 18:19 lists 450 prophets of Baal (and 400 prophets of the groves).

question: How many times did Elijah send his servant to look toward the sea before a cloud appeared?
ref_kjv: And said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times. And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Prepare thy chariot, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.
explanation: On the seventh time the servant saw a little cloud like a man's hand.

question: How was Elijah taken up into heaven?
ref_kjv: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
explanation: A chariot of fire appeared and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

question: Who was cast into the den of lions?
ref_kjv: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
explanation: King Darius commanded, and they cast Daniel into the den of lions.

question: Which king signed the decree that led to Daniel being thrown to the lions?
ref_kjv: Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.
explanation: King Darius signed the writing and the decree.

question: How many times a day did Daniel kneel to pray?
ref_kjv: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
explanation: Daniel kneeled upon his knees three times a day and prayed.

question: According to Daniel, how was he protected from the lions?
options: God sent His angel and shut their mouths
answer: God sent His angel and shut their mouths
ref_kjv: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
explanation: Daniel said, "My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths."

question: Which three young men were cast into the fiery furnace?
ref_kjv: And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
explanation: These three fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.

question: Which queen approached the king uninvited to save her people?
ref_kjv: And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
explanation: When the king saw Esther, she obtained favour and he held out the golden sceptre.

question: What did the king hold out to welcome Esther?
ref_kjv: And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
explanation: Holding out the golden sceptre meant the visitor would live (Esther 4:11).

question: Who raised Esther and urged her to act?
ref_kjv: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.
explanation: Mordecai brought up Esther, "his uncle's daughter."

question: Who plotted to destroy all the Jews in the Persian empire?
ref_kjv: And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.
explanation: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom of Ahasuerus.

question: What is the name of the Persian king in the book of Esther (KJV)?
ref_kjv: Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this is Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia, over an hundred and seven and twenty provinces:)
explanation: The book opens in the days of Ahasuerus, who reigned from India to Ethiopia.

question: Which feast commemorates the deliverance in the book of Esther?
ref_kjv: Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,
explanation: "They called these days Purim after the name of Pur."

question: In which town was Jesus born?
ref_kjv: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judæa, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
explanation: Joseph and Mary went to Bethlehem, where Mary brought forth her firstborn son and laid him in a manger.

question: Who announced the birth of Jesus to the shepherds?
ref_kjv: And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid. And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
explanation: The angel of the Lord said, "Unto you is born this day... a Saviour."

question: Why was the baby laid in a manger?
options: There was no room in the inn
answer: There was no room in the inn
ref_kjv: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
explanation: Luke 2:7 explains there was no room for them in the inn.

question: Which ruler's decree brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem?
ref_kjv: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Cæsar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.
explanation: A decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be taxed.

question: Which gifts did the wise men bring?
ref_kjv: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
explanation: They presented gifts: gold, and frankincense, and myrrh. Scripture does not say how many wise men there were.

question: According to Luke, who was governor of Syria at the time of the taxing?
ref_kjv: ( And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.)
explanation: Luke 2:2: "This taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria."

question: Which teaching event does this scene represent?
ref_kjv: And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him: And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying,
explanation: Seeing the multitudes, Jesus went up into a mountain and taught them.

question: "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit..."
ref_kjv: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
explanation: Matthew 5:5 promises the meek shall inherit the earth.

question: Jesus told His listeners, "Ye are the salt of the..."
ref_kjv: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.
explanation: Matthew 5:13: "Ye are the salt of the earth."

question: Which prayer did Jesus teach within the Sermon on the Mount?
ref_kjv: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
explanation: "After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven..."

question: In Jesus' illustration, on what did the wise man build his house?
ref_kjv: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
explanation: The wise man built his house upon a rock; the foolish man built upon the sand.

question: Which event does this stormy scene show?
ref_kjv: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
explanation: Jesus rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Peace, be still."

question: What did Jesus say to the wind and the sea?
ref_kjv: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
explanation: The wind ceased and there was a great calm.

question: Where was Jesus when the storm arose in Mark's account?
options: Asleep on a pillow in the stern
answer: Asleep on a pillow in the stern
ref_kjv: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
explanation: He was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow.

question: Which parable does this scene illustrate?
ref_kjv: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
explanation: A Samaritan had compassion on him and bound up his wounds.

question: Which two travellers passed by on the other side?
ref_kjv: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.
explanation: First a priest and then a Levite passed by on the other side.

question: On which road was the man attacked?
ref_kjv: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
explanation: "A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves."

question: Which question prompted Jesus to tell this parable?
ref_kjv: But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?
explanation: A lawyer, willing to justify himself, asked, "And who is my neighbour?"

question: How many pence did the Samaritan give the innkeeper?
ref_kjv: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
explanation: He took out two pence and gave them to the host.

question: What did the Samaritan pour into the man's wounds?
ref_kjv: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
explanation: He bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine.

question: Which parable does this reunion illustrate?
ref_kjv: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
explanation: The father saw him a great way off, ran, fell on his neck and kissed him.

question: What work did the younger son take in the far country?
ref_kjv: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
explanation: A citizen of that country sent him into his fields to feed swine.

question: What did the father call for when his son returned?
options: The best robe, a ring and shoes
answer: The best robe, a ring and shoes
ref_kjv: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
explanation: "Bring forth the best robe... put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet."

question: Who was angry and would not go in to the celebration?
ref_kjv: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
explanation: The elder son "was angry, and would not go in."

question: Which animal was killed for the welcome feast?
ref_kjv: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
explanation: "Bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry."

question: Which event does this upper-room scene depict?
ref_kjv: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
explanation: On the day of Pentecost cloven tongues like as of fire sat upon each of them.

question: What appeared and rested upon each of them?
options: Cloven tongues like as of fire
answer: Cloven tongues like as of fire
ref_kjv: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
explanation: Acts 2:3 describes cloven tongues like as of fire.

question: Which apostle stood up and preached to the crowd that day?
ref_kjv: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:
explanation: Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice.

question: About how many souls were added that day?
ref_kjv: Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.
explanation: Acts 2:41 reports about three thousand souls added. (Five thousand is Acts 4:4.)

question: Which apostle survived this shipwreck while being taken to Rome?
ref_kjv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape. But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
explanation: The centurion, willing to save Paul, kept the soldiers from their purpose, and all escaped safe to land.

question: On which island did the shipwrecked company land?
ref_kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
explanation: "They knew that the island was called Melita" (commonly identified with Malta).

question: What fastened on Paul's hand as he gathered sticks on the island?
ref_kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
explanation: A viper came out of the heat and fastened on his hand, but he felt no harm.

question: Which city was Paul finally brought to as a prisoner?
ref_kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
explanation: "When we came to Rome... Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier."

question: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?
ref_kjv: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
explanation: The LORD prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah.

question: How long was Jonah inside the fish?
ref_kjv: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
explanation: Jesus later referred to this sign in Matthew 12:40.

question: To which city did God send Jonah?
ref_kjv: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
explanation: "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it."

question: Where was Jonah trying to flee?
ref_kjv: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.
explanation: Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.

question: What plant did God prepare to shade Jonah?
ref_kjv: And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.
explanation: The LORD God prepared a gourd to be a shadow over his head.

question: Which morning does this scene depict?
options: The resurrection morning at the empty tomb
answer: The resurrection morning at the empty tomb
ref_kjv: And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun. And they said among themselves, Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great.
explanation: Very early on the first day of the week the women saw that the stone was rolled away.

question: What were the women bringing to the tomb?
ref_kjv: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.
explanation: They had bought sweet spices that they might come and anoint him.

question: According to Mark 16:9, to whom did the risen Jesus appear first?
ref_kjv: Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.
explanation: Mark 16:9 says he appeared first to Mary Magdalene. Note: many scholars regard Mark 16:9-20 as a later addition, though it appears in the KJV.

question: On which day of the week did the women come to the tomb?
options: The first day of the week
answer: The first day of the week
ref_kjv: And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun.
explanation: They came very early in the morning the first day of the week.
